notes: The Dam arena is the largest multiplayer stage in the game by pad count, and it is almost entirely outdoors: a long dam wall, guard towers and open approaches.

DATA CAVEAT: this stage exports its prop records as raw words that the extractor cannot yet walk cleanly, so there is no pickup census for it. Its pads and geometry are reliable; nothing here claims an armour or ammunition count, and any entry that would need one is marked community rather than verified.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: This is the biggest multiplayer stage in the game, so two-player matches are mostly searching and it needs a full complement to play well.
nuance.because: Four hundred and fourteen pads, more than any other arena including Caverns.

nuance.claim: The dam wall is a long straight run with no cover along most of its length, so crossing it in the open is the single most reliable way to die here.
The guard towers overlook the wall and its approaches, so holding one covers a large share of the map's movement.
A tower has one way in and no way out, so a strong position becomes a death sentence the moment someone brings an explosive to it.
The long outdoor sightlines make precision weapons dominant, more so than on any other stage.
The interiors at either end are the only places to break contact, so a losing fight is taken indoors rather than run from along the wall.
The open ground gives explosives distance to travel safely, and they are the answer to anyone holding a tower.
Mines are wasted in the open, so their placements are the building doorways and tower stairs, which are the only forced paths on the stage.
One-hit kills across a huge outdoor map produce long standoffs, since nobody can cross open ground and everyone can see most of it.
The size means an unarmed carrier can stay away from pursuit for a long time, so a single good hold can decide the match.
